settings.netflow.text: Your firewall or router can report the traffic of every device (NetFlow v5, v9 or IPFIX). Lanloom books it per country like its own connections and keeps only country, device and bytes. Off by default; Lanloom never sends anything to the router.

setup.guide.family.title: Create a read-only key
setup.guide.hub.1: Open the hub's web page and sign in.
setup.guide.hub.2: Optionally create a separate user for Lanloom that is not an administrator.
setup.guide.hub.3: In that user's profile, create a long-lived access token and copy it right away (it is shown only once).
setup.guide.hub.4: Enter the hub address and paste the token below, then press Test.
setup.guide.hub.title: Create an access token
setup.guide.hv.1: Open the hypervisor's web page and sign in as an administrator.
setup.guide.hv.2: Create an API token for a user, with privilege separation switched on.
setup.guide.hv.3: Give the token only the built-in auditor (read-only) role on the root path; Lanloom refuses tokens that can change anything.
setup.guide.hv.4: Enter the address, the token ID and the secret below, then press Test.
setup.guide.hv.title: Create a read-only API token
setup.guide.mqtt.1: Open the broker's configuration or its user management.
setup.guide.mqtt.2: Add a user for Lanloom with a password of its own.
setup.guide.mqtt.3: Allow it to read (subscribe to) the topics only, not to publish.
setup.guide.mqtt.4: Enter host, port, user name and password below (TLS if the broker uses it), then press Test.
setup.guide.mqtt.title: Create a read-only user
setup.guide.readonly: Lanloom only reads. Credentials are stored encrypted and are never shown again.
setup.guide.snmp.1: Open the web page of the router or switch and find the SNMP settings.
setup.guide.snmp.2: Switch SNMP on; prefer version 3 with a user, authentication and encryption.
setup.guide.snmp.3: Grant read-only access, ideally only for the address of this host.
setup.guide.snmp.4: Enter the device address and the community or the version 3 user below, then press Test.
setup.guide.snmp.title: Allow read-only SNMP
setup.reason.title: Web page title matches
setup.suggest.lead: From what the scan saw (open ports, page titles, announcements), these devices can tell Lanloom more. Lanloom never tries to sign in on its own.
setup.suggest.none: No known service was found. You can still add a source under ‘Other sources’.
setup.suggest.title: Suggested for your network

storage.err.choice: This value is not one of the offered choices.
storage.keep.lead: Older data is removed in the nightly clean-up. Shorter times keep the database small on a small host; longer times allow longer looks back.
storage.keep.title: How long data is kept
storage.kind.audit_days.hint: Who changed what. The same setting as under Security.
storage.kind.availability_days.hint: Devices offline and back, uplink outages, connection failures. At least 35 days, and never shorter than the reports need.
storage.kind.live_min.hint: Per-second samples behind the traffic charts. Kept in memory only; longer needs more RAM.
storage.kind.paths_days.hint: Daily bytes per device and country (the 30-day view needs at least 31 days).
storage.kind.paths_hours.hint: Hourly bytes per device and country (the 24-hour view needs at least one day).
storage.kind.reports_days.hint: The same setting as under Reports.
storage.kind.scans_keep.hint: Finished network scans kept in the list; devices found stay in the inventory.
storage.mem.lead: What Lanloom holds in memory right now.
storage.mem.live_value: {n} samples on {traces, plural, one {# trace} other {# traces}} (about {size})
storage.mem.title: Memory
storage.no_dbstat: This build of the database cannot report sizes per area; the entries are counted instead.
storage.report.full_soon: At the current growth ({growth} per day) the data volume is full in about {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. Shorten the retention under Settings › Storage or free space.
storage.report.no_room: The database ({size}) could not be compacted: not enough free disk space for a copy.
storage.report.ran: Nightly clean-up at {at}: {n, plural, one {# old entry} other {# old entries}} removed, {freed} freed.
storage.report.title: Storage
storage.run.lead: Every night after 03:00 Lanloom removes what is past its retention, refreshes the database statistics and compacts the file when a sixth of it is free.
storage.run.summary: {n, plural, one {# old entry} other {# old entries}} removed, {freed} freed, took {dur}
storage.run.title: Nightly clean-up
storage.space.lead: How much of the database each kind of data takes. Inventory and accounts are never removed automatically.
storage.space.title: Space used
storage.vacuum.failed: failed, will be tried again next night
storage.vacuum.no_room: skipped: not enough free disk space for a copy of the file
storage.wal: {size} of it in the write-ahead log
tfa.app.off: Codes from an app on your phone (any app for time-based one-time codes).
tfa.app.off_confirm: Turn off the authenticator app? Sign-in then only asks for the password (or a passkey).
tfa.app.on: Set up: sign-in asks for a 6-digit code.
tfa.lead: A second factor protects your account even if somebody learns the password.
tfa.passkey_counts: A passkey counts as a strong second factor too.
tfa.required: Your role requires a second factor. Please set one up now.
tfa.required_by: Your role requires a second factor. Set one up by {when}; after that the next sign-in asks for it first.
tfa.title: Two-step sign-in
topo.err.loop: That would put the device below itself.
topo.loop: {source} says {where}. That would close a loop and is ignored.
topo.manual.lead: For devices that no source can see, for example behind a simple switch or an access point without management. A manual entry always has priority.
topo.manual.title: Connected via (manual)
topo.reason.ap_default: It hangs on an access point and no source knows the link type, so it is shown as wireless. Set it by hand to change that.
topo.reason.behind: It shares port {port} with {via}, so it sits behind that device.
topo.reason.behind_ap: It shares port {port} with {via}, an access point, so it sits behind that device and is shown as wireless. Set it by hand to change that.
topo.reason.guest: A virtual network card behind port {port}, the same port as {via}: a guest on that host.
topo.reason.hypervisor: The hypervisor reports it as a guest of this host, network card on {port}.
topo.reason.shared: It shares port {port} with {n, plural, one {# other device} other {# other devices}}, maybe through a simple switch.
topo.rule: Order of precedence: manual entry, hypervisor, switch controller, LLDP, switch address table.
topo.title: Connection
topo.unknown: Port {port}: {n, plural, one {# more address that is} other {# more addresses that are}} not in the device list
totp.open_app: Open in an app on this device
totp.qr_label: QR code for the authenticator app
totp.step1: Open an authenticator app on your phone.
totp.step2: Scan the code, or type the key by hand.
totp.step3: Enter the 6-digit code the app shows.

users.delete_confirm: Delete {user}? The account, its sessions and second factors are removed; the audit log keeps its entries.
users.err.last_admin: At least one admin must stay.
users.err.proxy: This account signs in through the sign-in proxy; its password is managed there.
users.err.self: You cannot do that to your own account.
users.invite.lead: An invitation link lets one person create an account with the chosen role. It works once and expires after 24 hours.
users.invite.title: Invite someone
users.lead: Who can sign in, with which role. Changes take effect at once.
users.link_once: Send this link yourself (chat, mail, in person). It works once and only Lanloom knows its fingerprint.
users.name: Name
users.reset.clear_2fa: Also remove the second factor (lost phone)
users.reset.lead: Creates a one-time link (24 hours) with which the person sets a new password. Their sessions end when they use it.
users.reset.title: Reset the password of {user}
users.roles_hint: Viewer: look only · Operator: drafts, renaming, scans · Admin: settings, credentials, users, approvals, AI, updates.
users.title: Users
wizard.account.code_text: It is printed in the container log on first start (and stored in setup-code.txt in the data volume). On the command line:
wizard.account.lead: Lanloom always asks for a sign-in. The first account needs the one-time setup code from the container log, so nobody else on your network can claim this instance.
wizard.account.mismatch: The two passwords are not the same.
wizard.account.title: Create your account
wizard.connect.safety: All connections are read-only by design. Credentials are stored encrypted in the data volume and are never shown again.
wizard.connect.title: Connect more sources (optional)
wizard.done.lead: Two last choices. Both can be changed later in Settings.
wizard.done.title: Your map is ready
wizard.networks.isolated_text: It cannot see your home network directly, so device announcements will not be found. For full discovery start the container with host networking (see the install guide). You can still enter your network range below.
wizard.networks.isolated_title: Lanloom runs in an isolated container network
wizard.networks.manual_hint: Private ranges only, at most 1024 addresses (/22).
wizard.networks.none: No local network was detected. Add your network range below.
wizard.networks.pick_one: Please choose at least one network.
wizard.networks.title: Which networks belong to you?
wizard.passkey.lead: Sign in with your fingerprint, face or device PIN next time. You can always use the password as well.
wizard.passkey.title: Add a passkey?
wizard.review.lead: Each device was sorted automatically: {sure} sure, {probable} probable, {unknown} unknown. Rename or re-sort anything that looks wrong — you can change it later, too.
wizard.review.none: No devices were found. Check the selected network and that Lanloom uses host networking.
wizard.review.title: {n, plural, one {# device} other {# devices}} found
wizard.scan.addresses: {done} of {total, plural, one {# address} other {# addresses}}
wizard.scan.consent: I own this network or have permission to scan it.
wizard.scan.deep_text: Additionally checks about 200 common ports per device. Takes longer and may show up in the logs of security devices.
wizard.scan.fineprint: Lanloom only scans private address ranges you selected, never the internet, and never tries to log in anywhere.
wizard.scan.gentle_1: Reads the neighbour table of this host
wizard.scan.gentle_3: Checks 27 well-known service ports per device
wizard.scan.gentle_4: Rate-limited to about 40 connections per second
